rationale: The Court is likely to issue a narrow, administrable opinion holding that the ordinary dies-non/time-computation backdrop (reinforced by INA-era regulatory definitions and historical practice) means a statutory “period” ending on a weekend/holiday runs to the next business day, without endorsing tolling or discretionary extensions. Roberts is the most likely assignee to keep the ruling cabined and hold the broad coalition, with a substantial chance of a Gorsuch or Thomas opinion emphasizing the historical/textual canon and an Alito solo dissent stressing Dada-style strictness and the substantive nature of the departure obligation.
